Royal Mint sees record silver and platinum sales, renewed gold demand despite higher prices and rising bond yields
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold and silver faced significant headwinds through the summer as persistent inflation and higher bond yields raised the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets. However, some investors continued to see value in the precious metals, according to the latest sales figures from the British Royal Mint. On Wednesday, the Royal Mint announced record year-to-date silver and platinum sales and renewed demand for gold bullion. The Mint does not publish exact bullion sales figures but said that revenue from silver bullion surged in the first three quarters of 2026. “ Silver bullion purchases on royalmint.com increased by 295% during the first nine months of 2026, compared with the same period in 2025. P latinum bullion revenue also rose by 118%, with both metals surpassing every previous full-year total, with a quarter of the calendar year still remaining,” the Mint said in the report. “Silver bullion coins have been particularly popular, with revenue increasing by 323% year-on-year across the first three quarters. The figures point to growing interest in silver as investors explore different ways to hold physical precious metals, including UK bullion coins.”

Russia sells 6.2 tonnes of gold in September as bullion reserves fall to lowest level since 2019
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Russia sold 200,000 troy ounces of gold in September, equivalent to 6.2 tonnes, according to the latest figures released by the Bank of Russia. Last month’s bullion sales lowered Russia’s sovereign gold holdings to 72.8 million troy ounces, or 2,264 tonnes, their lowest level since the end of 2019. Russia is in the midst of its largest sustained drawdown in gold reserves since the financial crisis of 1998, with the country liquidating around 62 tonnes of the precious metal since December 2025 as the government struggles to finance a ballooning federal budget deficit.

items.titleEn: EU probes Booking.com over online fraud risks
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: The European Union opened an investigation into online travel agent Booking.com on Wednesday over alleged failures to tackle fake listings and phishing scams. The EU fears Booking.com has underestimated the impact of fraud and unlicensed accommodation, and is not sufficiently protecting users' data from being misused for scams.

items.titleEn: Nvidia CEO encourages Europe's lagging AI sector and offers tools to accelerate data center buildout
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urged players in Europe's lagging artificial intelligence industry to get going and touted a modular system to quickly build AI data centers he says are sorely needed by developers on the continent. In an upbeat speech Wednesday at a company conference for developers and investors in Berlin, Huang also laid out tools to keep AI applications from running amok by confining them in a digital "sandbox."
